title: One dead as brawl breaks out at Y-Zet gig
note: KEY CORRECTION: the 10 June 2017 Mandalay death was NOT a beef killing. The fatal fight began when two groups accidentally elbowed each other while dancing in a packed crowd at a FREE album-promotion concert; four attackers aged 17-20 beat a 19-year-old with a two-foot steel pipe. Eight police and 30 private security were on duty; a friend filed under ss.114 and 302. Six years separate the ~2011 Shwee Die track from the 2017 death. Do not encode a causal relationship.

title: Myanmar Hip Hop's Revolution (9KT and MK)
note: Documents 9KT and MK as masked, pseudonymous Generation Wave-affiliated artists who produced in Mae Sot, Thailand for safety, and 9KT's 11-track album 'Never Give Up' (Oct 2016). DO NOT attempt to de-anonymise either. A DIFFERENT article from the swagger-math piece already in sources.

title: DJs, club owner and manager arrested for disrespectful Buddha-song mix in Mandalay
note: 31 July 2025, Cover Club, Mahaaungmye Township, Mandalay. Charged under s.505(a), case (P)214/2025, Myoma PS. Single-source quoting the Myanmar Police Force. Evidence that the legal architecture reaches non-rap music in Mandalay.

title: Artistes held for attempting to disrupt democratic election
note: Law enacted 29 July 2025; arrests from 27-29 Oct 2025 under SAC Law No. 48/2025, penalties 3 years to death. Mostly film and comedy rather than hip-hop, but the same legal architecture that catches rappers.

title: Sham election law and freedom of expression in Myanmar
note: 32 named individuals arrested under the election law by 14 Nov 2025; the junta claimed 88 charged by 29 Oct; Reuters reported at least 229 by Dec 2025. Figures diverge by counting method.

title: Myanmar arrests hundreds under new election law ahead of December vote
In-depth: Myanmar pro-military Telegram channels are doxxing critics
note: CORRECTION: the archive's earlier note dated this March 2025. The investigation is 22 Aug 2023 and the arrest was 24 May 2023. Documents 32 arrests in Jan-May 2023 from Ka Ka Han posts alone, and a FOEIM school data leak of hundreds of students' details. SAFETY: this is the documented mechanism behind Byu Har's arrest - do not publish specific channel handles or personal details.

title: Artistic creation without naming names

title: Burmese rapper banned from performing
note: CORRECTION: this was a one-year ban by the Myanmar Music Association, NOT an arrest. G-Tone was handcuffed after leaving the stage but not detained; police then beat audience members, escalating it into a riot. SAFETY: the tattoo's content is DISPUTED - DVB says a back tattoo of clasped praying hands, while de Bakker quoting Yan Yan Chan says rosary beads on a wrist. Coconuts (2015) separately garbles this as a 2008 arrest, wrong on both year and sanction.

title: The Beat of Yangon
author: Jeroen de Bakker
note: Key reporting on the 2007-08 scene: artists slandered, banned and arrested on stage for their lyrics; Acid's Beginning had 16 tracks of which the censor board passed 11; the copy-track economy; and underground-vs-mainstream self-policing.

title: Will copyright problems be solved? (Myanmar film and song copy rights)
note: The most important structural frame for this archive: Thar Si Thaw of the Myanmar Music Association testifies that existing law 'cannot give the necessary protection', so a credit dispute here is usually not a quarrel between artists but an absent legal category.

title: Mock stars: Myanmar's pop plagiarists
note: Documents the 'copy thachin' (copy song) genre as a product of the state's cultural quarantine, including Lay Phyu's Metallica rewrite known domestically as 'Exits'.

title: Rap Against Junta: A Propaganda War Machine for Freedom (Ko Aye Win on the battle form)
author: Shwe Lan Ga Lay
note: The cleanest documented beef analogue in the archive: DICKCOUNCIL producer Ko Aye Win explains deliberately turning the battle form away from other rappers and onto the junta. The host frames it as repurposing an adversarial form against a target not used to being spoken to that way.

title: Y-Zet (full article with discography)
note: The fuller Y-Zet record. Known errors in it: birthplace is Pyin Oo Lwin (Mandalay Region), not Mandalay city; the infobox reads 'Member of: Oasix' on a solo artist; the Burmese letter za is glossed as 'Gene'; and the 'Shwee Die beefing' wording rests on a single now-dead Burmese source whose word choice conflicts with a Korean mirror.

title: SAC issues warrants under s.505(a) for 20 individuals including G Fatt
note: Primary-adjacent: publishes the State Administration Council announcement. Also the source for a separate 2 April list of ~20 more names under s.505(a).

title: Phyo Zeya Thaw
note: Documents the March 2008 arrest, the November 2008 sentence under SLORC Law 6/88 plus a foreign-currency charge, the 17 May 2011 release, his own pre-sentencing and post-release statements, and the August 2011 performance ban. See also the Daily Beast's anonymous-sourced resistance-role claim, recorded separately in disputes.json as unresolved.
